I made $1,900 in spiffs this month and @bot did most of the grunt work

I'm the F5 guy where I work. F5 has an SE incentive program that pays you for enablement work. $100 every time you train an internal sales team. $200 for every customer workshop you host.

I've been doing this job for 3 years now. Last Fiscal Year (Oct-Sep) I earned a total of $1,850 in these spiffs. I was doing it manually and just a little here a little there in between the rest of the things keeping me busy. 

Last month I handed that part to Grok Bot. Here's what it did:

In September, I told it “find all the sales directors and solutions architect directors that work for my company using the directory in outlook & draft an email to them asking for 10-15 min on their next team call”

It found all 51 of them and left drafts in my outlook for me. I just proof read and hit send. 

It kept score. Every call got logged with the date, the team, and how many people were invited.

It then wrote the claims. It wrote the email to my F5 channel SE explaining why each activity qualifies, with every calendar invite attached and named.

Since Oct 1:
-15 internal sales trainings with my company’s sales and SA teams
-2 customer workshops that came out of those calls (one of them was a 5-hour whiteboarding session)
-$1,900 in spiffs earned

The money is great. It’s also great that 15 sales teams now know exactly when to bring me in. That's already turning into customer meetings & more spiffs opportunities for me. 

If there's work you keep putting off, like tracking, follow-ups, or getting paid for stuff you already did, that's where an AI assistant pays off the most for me and it’s worth $100 to try it out for a month

(It’s currently telling me who said yes but hasn’t sent an invite yet and went ahead and drafted a reply in outlook to bump it in their inbox reminding them to send me the meeting)

@bot is AWESOME and just funded itself for the next year.
